subject: OPEN statement
notes: RULE: 'Upon successful execution of the OPEN statement, the current volume pointer is set: a) To point to the first or only reel/unit in the physical file if INPUT or I-O is specified. b) To point to the reel/unit containing the last record in the physical file if EXTEND is specified. c) To point to the newly created reel/unit in the physical file for an unavailable file if EXTEND, I-O, or OUTPUT is specified.' cite.py --check 14.9.27.4: OK (§14.9.27.4 19)). DERIVATION: §9.1.10 (Current volume pointer) states 'The current volume pointer is a CONCEPTUAL ENTITY used in this document to facilitate exact specification of the current physical volume of a sequential file. The status of the current volume pointer is affected by the CLOSE, OPEN, READ, and WRITE statements.' (cite.py --check 9.1.10: OK) — it is not a programmer-visible register and has no COBOL surface. Its only observable consequences are reel/unit swaps (§14.9.30.4 GR23 READ, §14.9.51.4 GR24 WRITE) and CLOSE unit processing (§14.9.6.4 Table 14). WiseOwl COBOL places every sequential physical file in §14.9.6.4 GR2 category (a) NON-UNIT, "A file whose input or output medium is such that the concepts of rewind and units have no meaning" (cite.py --check 14.9.6.4 'A file whose input or output medium is such that the concepts of rewind and units have no meaning': OK GR2 a)), and every relative or indexed file in (d) Non-sequential; never in (b) 'A sequential file that is entirely contained on one unit' (cite.py --check 14.9.6.4 'A sequential file that is entirely contained on one unit': OK GR2 b)). The placement is FORCED rather than chosen: §9.1.13.2 item 6 defines the '07' the compiler reports for CLOSE ... REEL/UNIT, CLOSE ... WITH NO REWIND and OPEN ... WITH NO REWIND as the status of a statement that "references a physical file on a non-reel/unit medium" (cite.py --check 9.1.13.2 'references a physical file on a non-reel/unit medium': OK item 6)), and Table 14 prints symbol g (the '07') in the Non-unit column alone. The determination is written in docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 7 (A.1 item 24, DOC-A.1-24) and realized as FileConnector.Category / CloseTable14.cs; FileRegistry.CloseReelUnit and CloseNoRewind are its '07' sites. A category (a) file has NO unit for a current volume pointer to designate (the pointer exists 'to facilitate exact specification of the current physical volume of a sequential file', section 9.1.10), and a category (d) file is not a sequential file at all, so arms a), b) and c) name a reel/unit that does not exist and no state a program can observe would disagree with them: the rule imposes no implementation obligation. The verdict is the same if a file is read as having one conceptual unit (all three arms then designate it), so it does not rest on the category; the CATEGORY is only what a reader needs to cite when asked why the OPEN-side volume pointer is not modelled. TEST: unit:CloseTable14Tests.Category_PlacesEverySupportedConnectorKind pins the placement (a)/(d) per connector kind, and unit:FileStatusDisciplineTests.CloseReelUnit_AbsentOptional_NoUnitProcessing pins the non-unit CLOSE REEL/UNIT cell (successful, no unit processing, '07'). GR-14.9.27.4-11 (OPEN ... NO REWIND = '07') is the OPEN-side twin of the same medium determination and has landed (kb/Work PB317); the two rows now agree. Re-derived by kb/Work PB604, which replaced this row's earlier 'single-unit / exactly ONE reel/unit' wording (category (b), which the reported '07' contradicts) and retired its stale warning that the GR11 arm was missing and that docs/CONFORMANCE.md stated the opposite. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 · 2002 · 2014 · 2023
